text: At the mans heels trotted a dog, a big gray husky that looked just like its brother, the wild wolf. <break time="0.8s" /> The dog knew by instinct that it was no time for traveling, for it was really seventy five degrees below zero. <break time="0.8s" /> It walked close behind the man and watched his every move, as if it expected him to stop and build a fire. <break time="0.8s" /> He walked carefully along the frozen creek, for he knew that some springs under the snow never froze, even in the coldest weather. <break time="0.8s" /> Once the dog broke through into the water, and the man pulled off his mitten to tear the ice from its feet. <break time="0.8s" /> He bared his fingers for less than a minute, but he was astonished at how quickly they became numb. <break time="0.8s" /> At half past twelve he reached the forks of the creek, where he stopped to eat his lunch. <break time="0.8s" /> But the ice around his mouth would not let him bite the biscuit, for he had forgotten to build a fire first. <break time="0.8s" /> He remembered the old timer on Sulphur Creek, who had told him how cold it could get, and he had laughed at him at the time. <break time="0.8s" /> So he built a small fire, and sitting by its warmth, he ate his biscuits while the dog lay happily near the flames.
